purpose: Check whether Python, Rust, mixed-language, and future-language discoveries stay pointer-only, route to the right DAD asset, and require local proof before promotion.

expected: candidate route includes Python advantage assets or coding tactics radar
does not copy generated counterexamples into DAD mail
fail_if: the case is promoted as reviewed without local outcome evidence
the case stores raw private inputs

expected: requires profile evidence and same-scope parity before timing claims
routes to Rust buildout guide only as a cautionary candidate
fail_if: the case recommends a downstream Rust rewrite
the case claims speed without same-workload timing
the case treats popularity or novelty as proof

given: safe_summary=contains copied documentation or private repo rows
expected: reject copied docs, copied source blobs, private rows, secrets, raw logs, and long benchmark excerpts
allow only pointer, hash, short summary, applicability limits, and validation idea
fail_if: external text is stored as DAD source truth
private-origin content can flow to public-facing repos without human release
redaction count is treated as proof of safety

given: safe_summary=new language may help AI coding
expected: create or keep candidate-only future-language row
require compiler, linter, type checker, test runner, fuzzer, profiler, package auditor, runtime tracer, or schema validator
require at least one negative or failure example
fail_if: the language becomes recommendable from popularity alone
the record lacks a harness or validation route

must_not_claim: This harness proves a technique is state of the art.
A trusted source tier authorizes copying docs or code.
A language-frontier candidate overrides repo-local style, tests, security, source authority, or human gates.
promotion_gate: Promote only after source screening, local validation or harness outcome, applicability limits, rejection signals, and postflight/usage feedback.
